[23/06/2026 10:45 pm] 0_____________________________.0
Here's my take, past the condescending messages and fallacies: 

I always quote this personal anecdote; "Awareness of death is what gives life meaning"

I think it's contradictory in every perspective whether death is Good or bad. I'm not here to discuss whether death is good or bad because in these contexts, good or bad is not defined. Judgement can only be extrapolated based on an individual's belief and/or assumption of perception of death itself. 

To question death itself is a mistake. It's a fact.  Inherently death serves no meaning other than to limit the existence of human individuals. However you try to interpret that is beyond the scope of the argument unless you want to hold two arguments at once; this has been a ongoing debate of theologists and philosophers for thousands of years till now. 


If you want my take on the arguments you yourselves make, then I'd have to take Jad's side, not because he's correct, but because he speaks within the scope of the argument he presents himself. He is simply "more correct" in this area. 

If we're talking about the nature of the arguments for and against death, then the arguments become unfalsifiable in the eyes of the beholder. Rather than discussion about death, a more meaningful debate would be to discuss the meaning of life. 

Hope this helps.
